contentBlocks.text: Last week you explored matter and chemical reactions. This week: a new topic, energy!

Kinetic energy is the energy of motion — a moving car, a thrown ball, flowing water all have kinetic energy. Potential energy is stored energy based on position or condition — a ball held above the ground, a stretched rubber band, or a compressed spring all have potential energy, ready to be released. Classify these as kinetic or potential: a rock sitting at the edge of a cliff, a rock rolling down a hill.
You just classified kinetic and potential energy! Tomorrow we'll learn how energy transfers between objects.

objectives: Define kinetic energy as the energy of motion and potential energy as stored energy
Correctly classify a stationary cliff-edge rock (potential) and a rolling rock (kinetic)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's matter/chemical-reactions work briefly.
2. Introduce kinetic and potential energy with real examples.
3. Have the child classify the two rock scenarios.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's energy-transfer lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a simple physical demonstration — holding a ball still (potential) then dropping it (kinetic) — to make the distinction concrete
Ready for more: ask the child to think of a real example where an object has both kinetic and potential energy at the same time
Opens this week's energy thread from the course's own description, using classic, well-established physics examples
teacherGuide.answerKey: The rock at the cliff edge has potential energy (stored, based on position). The rolling rock has kinetic energy (energy of motion).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 6-8 Physical Science standard MS-PS3-1: relationship between kinetic energy and mass/speed, opening this week's energy thread.
